SPECIAL MEETING AGENDA - UPDATED
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
MONDAY - NOVEMBER 27, 2023 - 07:00 P.M.
CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL CHAMBER
18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CA 90703
COUNCILMEMBER YOKOYAMA WILL PARTICIPATE VIA TELECONFERENCE FROM THE HILTON GARDEN INN HOTEL, 1225 FIRST STREET NE, WASHINGTON, DISTRICT OF COLUMBIA, 20002, ROOM #1306, AND THIS AGENDA WILL BE POSTED AT THAT LOCATION IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE CALIFORNIA GOVERNMENT CODE
Agenda Materials
The complete agenda for this meeting is available on-demand at www.cerritos.us and at the Office of the City Clerk, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, 1st floor, Cerritos, CA, during regular business hours (Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., weekend and observed holidays excepted). Any materials submitted to the legislative body after distribution of this agenda will be available for public inspection in the Office of the City Clerk during regular business hours. Requests for agenda materials or meeting participation assistance can also be made by email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by phone at (562) 916-1248 during regular business hours.
PUBLIC OBSERVATION AND PARTICIPATION
The public can observe the meeting via livestream on the City’s website at www.cerritos.us, on cable television at Cerritos TV3, or in person in the Council Chamber.
Public Comments
Members of the public may provide public comment for this meeting in person at the meeting or by using the following alternate methods:
Written correspondence (hard copy or email): Public comments can be submitted via email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by hard copy to the Office the City Clerk no later than 3:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Please identify the agenda item number in the subject line of the email or hard copy document. All written correspondence received by the 3:00 p.m. deadline will be distributed to the legislative body prior to the meeting. During the meeting, your name and summary comments will be read into the record. The document will be retained with the public record of the meeting.
Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Accommodations
In compliance with the ADA, any person with a disability who requires accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the Office of the City Clerk at (562) 916-1248 to request accommodation. The City will use its best efforts to provide reasonable accommodations related to the meeting.

During this part of the meeting members of the City Council report to the community on various matters of interest, including reports concerning committees on which the Councilmembers serve and reports on meetings/conferences attended. MINUTES OF A SPECIAL MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE SUCCESSOR
AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD MONDAY, NOVEMBER 27,
2023, 7:00 P.M., IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBER AT CERRITOS CITY HALL, 18125 BLOOMFIELD
AVENUE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA. COUNCILMEMBER YOKOYAMA PARTICIPATED VIA
TELECONFERENCE FROM THE HILTON GARDEN INN HOTEL, 1225 FIRST STREET NE,
WASHINGTON, DISTRICT OF COLUMBIA, 20002, ROOM #1306, AND THIS AGENDA WAS
POSTED AT THAT LOCATION IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE CALIFORNIA GOVERNMENT CODE.

 1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

 2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Vida Barone, City Clerk/Treasurer.

 3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by the Cerritos Joy of Singing Class.

 4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Lynda P. Johnson
  Council/Agency Member Chuong Vo
  Council/Agency Member Frank Aurelio Yokoyama (via teleconference)
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Naresh Solanki
  Mayor/Chair Bruce W. Barrows

 5.  Presentations/Appointments

  None.

  service) (COUNCIL).

  There were no public comments received on this item and no action was taken.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period. Noting there were no individuals who
  elected to provide public comment, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

  This item was pulled from the consent calendar by Councilmember Johnson for separate
  consideration.

  A staff report was given by Dario Simoes, Acting Director of Public Works/City Engineer.

  MOTION: It was moved by Vo, and seconded by Johnson, to:

  1. Continue the local emergency as proclaimed in Resolution No. 2023-05, at the Cerritos
  Iron-Wood Nine Golf Course and the nearby City property with the C-4 well site;

  2. Make the findings set forth in Sections one (1) through eight (8) of Resolution No.

  existence of a local emergency as specified; and

  3. Direct staff to provide a report to the City Council regarding the local emergency at
  least once every sixty (60) days, pursuant to Section 8630(c) of the California
  Government Code, until the City Council terminates the local emergency (COUNCIL).

  AYES:  Johnson, Vo, Yokoyama, Solanki, Barrows

  *Pursuant to Section 15301 of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Guidelines,

  MOTION: It was moved by Solanki, and seconded by Vo, to:

  1. Adopt findings in accordance with the California Environmental Quality Act, Public
  Resources Code Section 21000 et seq. (CEQA) that the improvements planned under
  the proposed contract award are categorically exempt pursuant to Section 15301 of the
  CEQA Guidelines, based on the findings set forth in the agenda report associated with
  this item;

  2. Award a contract in the amount of $163,000 to CJ Concrete Construction, Inc. for
  CDBG-funded curb ramp/sidewalk repairs at Cerritos Towne Center (total bid), Bid No.
  1532-23, and reject the other bids; and

  3. Authorize the City Manager or designee to execute any project-related change orders,
  in accordance with the City’s adopted Purchasing and Contracting Policy (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Johnson, Vo, Yokoyama, Solanki, Barrows
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

  *Pursuant to Section 15301 of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Guidelines,

  MOTION: It was moved by Solanki, and seconded by Vo, to:

  1. Adopt findings in accordance with the California Environmental Quality Act, Public

  2. Award one-year contracts, with provisions to extend up to four (4) one-year extensions

7G.  Authorization to proceed with open market proposal procurement for the Swim/Fitness
  Center rehabilitation boiler replacement, Project No. 20201 (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Solanki, and seconded by Vo, to:

  1. Pursuant to Section 3.20.060(h) of the Cerritos Municipal Code, determine that it is in
  the best interest of the City to dispense with bidding based on the findings set forth in
  the agenda report associated with this item; and

  2. Authorize City staff to dispense with the bidding process and proceed with open market
  proposal procurement for the Swim/Fitness Center Rehabilitation Boiler Replacement,
  Project No. 20201, and present a report to the City Council for review and consideration
  of award of contract for the subject project at a future meeting (COUNCIL).

  ABSENT:  None

8A.  Review and consideration to waive full reading of and adopt A RESOLUTION OF THE
  CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AUTHORIZING UTILIZATION OF RESTRICTED COMMUNITY

  RAMPS ALONG TOWNE CENTER DRIVE AND PARK PLAZA DRIVE WITHIN THE CERRITOS
  TOWNE CENTER (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Dario Simoes, Acting Director of Public Works/City Engineer. A
  PowerPoint presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public hearing and the public comments period. Noting there were
  no individuals who elected to provide public comment, the Mayor declared the public
  comments period and public hearing closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Solanki, and seconded by Johnson, to waive full reading of and
  adopt Resolution No. 2023-37, A RESOLUTION OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL
  AUTHORIZING UTILIZATION OF RESTRICTED COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT BLOCK
  GRANT (CDBG) FUNDS, TOTALING APPROXIMATELY $200,000, DURING FISCAL
  YEAR 2024-2025, TO CONSTRUCT AND RETROFIT ACCESSIBLE CURB RAMPS
  ALONG TOWNE CENTER DRIVE AND PARK PLAZA DRIVE WITHIN THE CERRITOS
  TOWNE CENTER (COUNCIL).

  proposal for Cerritos Center for the Performing Arts marketing analysis and assessment,

  A staff report was given by Annie Hylton, City Librarian and Marketing Manager.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

  David Pylman expressed his support for expanded and improved programming at the
  Cerritos Center for the Performing Arts, and his opposition to the utilization of electronic
  ticketing services for the facility.

  CCPA marketing analysis and assessment and services to market the theater’s
